REPORT ON trial of Joseph Rothman.

Made by D.S.I.Reeves. Forwarded by C.J. Bourke

Sir,
Joseph Rothman was yesterday at 2.15 P.M. brought up on
remand. The charge against him was withdrawn by the Crown,
and he was discharged. He was however immediately re-arrested
on the " China (War Powers) Order In Council 1917, and will be
brought before the Supreme Court on Thursday 5th Inst, for an
order of deportation to be made against. I am informed that
he will be deported to Singapore. At the Court yesterday
Rothman showed me a letter from Mr Rodgers, lawyer, in which
Miss Pollock demands the sum of $300.00 from Rothman for com-
pensation for libel and slander, failing the payment of this
sum an action to recover this amount would be started against
him.

I am Sir,

Made by D.S.I.Brewster. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.

Sir,
In accordance with instructions a Warrant to search the
above premises was applied for and executed by a Police Party
under myself at 4 p.m. on the 28th inst.
Nothing of a nature to support our information was found
but a small order book was found which showed that Q. Nielsen
had ordered a rubber stamp there in March 1915.
As the Management could not produce the book containing
a fac-simile of the stamp in question although they produced
fac-similes of other stamps ordered in 1915, I took the order
book to the Station and told the Manager that a full explanation
of the incident would be required by the Police by noon on
the following day.
The Manager is of opinion that owing to pressure of work
the job must have been sent to another firm, hence the
confusion.

Your obedient servant,
WBrewster.

Statement of Max Kindler, 8th June 1917.

I am a Dentist residing lately at 54 Nanking Road,
(above Boyes Basset & Co). I sold my office two months
ago to Dr.Cameron, since when I have been residing at 65
Broadway Terrace, but for the last two days at the French
Hotel.

I was born in Braila in Roumania in 1886, my father being
Austrian and my mother Dutch. I was educated in Vienna and
Berlin. I took my Dental Degrees in Berlin. After I got
my degrees I practiced in Vienna as an Assistant in 1906
for 8 months. From Vienna I went to Bucharest. I remained
in Bucharest for 13 or 14 months during the Exposition. In
Bucharest I was a Dental Surgeon assisting Dr.Lempard (Dentist
de la Court Royal). From Bucharest I travelled for about 5
months through the Holy Land, Turkey, Greece and Egypt. I
settled in Egypt (1908) where I was first an assistant to Dr.
Moser in Alexandria. After some time I became acquainted
with Lt.Col. Maxwell, R.A.M.C. and through his influence I
became a Dental Surgeon in the Mustapha Pasha Barracks Rahale
Alexandria. I was there for over a year. After that I went
to Madras, India. This was in November 1911. In Madras I
became Dental Surgeon to General Hospital in Madras, my
superior being Major Badcock R.A.M.C. I remained in this
employ for about 4 or 5 months and then I established myself
at Montrode, Madras. Major Badcock was displeased at my
leaving and only gave me a certificate "for a few weeks". I
remained in Madras until 1913 when I sold my goodwill to a
Dr.Halar for R.2000. From there I returned to Egypt, in
February 1913 where I was seeking employment but could not
get a suitable position. In the beginning of 1914 I bought
a whole Dental outfit at Alexandria(receipts produced).
I remained the whole time in either Alexandria or Cairo.
In the beginning of 1914 I went to Singapore and established
myself in Battery Road, Macallisters Building. I had spent

1917年7月2日

马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）的陈述，1917年6月8日。

我是一名牙医，最近居住在南京路54号，
（博伊斯·巴塞特公司（Boyes Basset & Co）楼上）。两个月前
我将诊所卖给了卡梅伦医生（Dr.Cameron），此后我一直居住在
百老汇大厦65号，但最近两天住在法兰西饭店。

我于1886年出生在罗马尼亚的布勒伊拉（Braila），父亲是
奥地利人，母亲是荷兰人。我在维也纳和柏林接受教育。我在柏林
获得了牙科学位。获得学位后，我于1906年在维也纳
作为一名助手执业了8个月。从维也纳我去了布加勒斯特。我在
布加勒斯特停留了13或14个月，正值博览会期间。在
布加勒斯特，我是一名牙科外科医生，协助伦帕德医生（Dr.Lempard）（皇家宫廷牙医
Dentist de la Court Royal）。从布加勒斯特我旅行了大约5
个月，途经圣地、土耳其、希腊和埃及。我
定居在埃及（1908年），起初在亚历山大港担任莫泽医生（Dr.
Moser）的助手。一段时间后，我结识了皇家陆军医疗 Corps（R.A.M.C.）的
麦克斯韦尔中校（Lt.Col. Maxwell），并通过他的影响，我成为
亚历山大港拉哈莱（Rahale）穆斯塔法帕夏兵营（Mustapha Pasha Barracks）的
牙科外科医生。我在那里待了一年多。之后我去了
印度马德拉斯。那是1911年11月。在马德拉斯，我成为
马德拉斯总医院的牙科外科医生，我的上级是皇家陆军医疗 Corps（R.A.M.C.）的
巴德科克少校（Major Badcock）。我受雇于此
大约4或5个月，然后在马德拉斯的蒙特罗德（Montrode）自立门户。
巴德科克少校对我不满
我离开，只给了我一份“几周”的证明。我
留在马德拉斯直到1913年，当时我将商誉以2000卢比的价格卖给了
哈拉尔医生（Dr.Halar）。从那里我返回埃及，在
1913年2月，我正在寻找工作，但未能
获得合适的职位。1914年初，我在亚历山大港购买了一整套
牙科设备（已出示收据）。
我一直待在亚历山大港或开罗。
1914年初，我去了新加坡，并在
电池路（Battery Road）的麦卡利斯特大楼（Macallisters Building）自立门户。我已花费

This was told me by several of my patients. I then went to

which was delivered to me was not what I had bought, I had
an argument with Ettinger. Since that time I had never
spoken to him. About 3 or 4 months later I heard that
Ettinger was in the employ of the German Consulate as a
secret service man. I heard that he was under Dr. Vorstmann
and was making Russian subjects, German protected subjects,
for payment. This was well known to the Police Authorities.
One day in the beginning of 1918 I was shown a Russian pass-
port, the filled-in portion of which had been washed with
acid so that it could be filled in by any person. This was
shown to me by a German client. He did not give me his real
name, and the passport was written in Russian, which language
I am unable to read. He asked my opinion about it. I saw
immediately that it was a washed passport, as the paper was
slightly damaged and the ink was fresh. I warned him, and
told him that it was too dangerous to run the risk, so he
went to the German Authorities and told them that it was too
dangerous for him to travel on that passport as it could be
clearly seen that it was forged. They asked him who had
told him that, and asked why he did not detect that when it
was given to him. Being an officer, he had to confess that
I had told him. I was then called to the German Chancellor
(Gatien) and he asked me for an explanation as to how I had
detected the forgery. I said that it was very poorly
done, and that if they could not do anything better than that
they should not put a person in a position of such risk.
He then asked me what they could do, as they had different
officers in Shanghai, Tientsin and Peking who had to be sent
home, some of whom had escaped from Siberian Camps; so I
told him to find original neutral passports and to print them
in Shanghai and work them out properly so as to make it im-
possible to detect a forgery. I then left. About a

我对它的看法。我立刻看出这是一本被清洗过的护照，因为纸张

身为一名军官，他不得不承认是

I asked him if he had his passport with him, and
he said No. I then asked him where it was and he said he
had left it in the Ward with his clothes. He returned
immediately to the Ward, and after about 10 minutes brought
his clothes with the passport. I handed over the passport
to the officer and we took Kobaka to the Tollefsen Hotel,
where we paid for his board and lodging for the time being.
As we had had no dinner, the officer invited me to Newman's
Restaurant where he we had dinner. The following day the officer
came in the morning and asked me if I had said anything about
printing to the German Authorities, and asked if this passport
could not be printed. I told him that unless the German
Consulate agreed to it, I would not do it. As I had seen with
my own eyes at G.Berthel's Office an similar passport(Russian)
also forged with the stamp, seal and signature in perfect
condition, which was a very good forgery, I thought the same
could be done with the Spanish passport. The officer went
away and took the passport with him. In the afternoon I was
called to the German Consulate when I was told that it was
quite safe and that I may do it for the man. The Officer
then told me that I could have it done for him and to go to
a Printer and he would pay all the expenses. I went to a
printer who carries on business opposite the Central Police
Station and he made all the paper stamps. It took him
4 or 5 days to do it. I can recognise the photograph which
was forged if I see it. I got back the original passport
filled in one blank pass with a typewriter as the original
was, ande returned the original to Kobaka for the use of his
passport. The officer gave Kobaka $50 and paid his Hotel
bill and paid my expenses which were about $38. This took
place in the early part of 1916 about March. At the same
time Mr.Berthel an Austrian, used to furnish the German
Authorities with forgeries of two visies, one made by the

我问他是否随身携带护照，他说没有。接着我问他护照在哪里，他说他把护照和衣服一起留在了病房里。他立即返回病房，大约10分钟后带着衣服和护照回来了。我将护照交给警官，随后我们将Kobaka带到托勒夫森旅馆（Tollefsen Hotel），并暂时为他支付了食宿费用。由于我们尚未吃晚饭，警官邀请我去纽曼餐厅（Newman's Restaurant），我们在那里用了晚餐。第二天早上，警官前来问我是否曾向德国当局提及印刷之事，并询问这本护照是否可以仿制印刷。我告诉他，除非德国领事馆同意，否则我不会这样做。因为我曾在G. Berthel的办公室里亲眼见过一本类似的（俄罗斯）护照，其印章、封记和签名均伪造得完好无缺，是一次非常精良的伪造，我认为西班牙护照也可以如法炮制。警官随即离开，并带走了护照。下午，我被召至德国领事馆，被告知此事十分安全，我可以为那人办理。于是警官告诉我，可以为他办理，让我去找一家印刷商，所有费用由他支付。我找到了一位在中央捕房对面经营的印刷商，他制作了所有的纸质印章。这项工作花费了他4到5天的时间。如果看到那张伪造的照片，我能辨认出来。我收回了原始护照，像原件一样用打字机填写了一张空白通行证，并将原件归还给Kobaka供其使用护照之需。警官给了Kobaka 50美元，支付了他的旅馆账单，并支付了我的开销，约为38美元。这件事发生在1916年初，大约在3月份。与此同时，奥地利人Berthel先生习惯于向德国当局提供两种签证的伪造品，一种是由

British Authorities and one by the Russian Authorities.
After that similar passports with visies were distributed
and photos were received from Peking and Tientsin and passports
were made in Shanghai by the German and Austrian Authorities
and returned to Peking and Tientsin and other places.
Afterwards the German Authorities thought that there were
too many Spanish passports in circulation, and that it was
safer to take another passport and to make it the same as
the Spanish one. They obtained a Norwegian passport.
I do not know how they got it. I obtained a copy of the
original. I obtained the original Norwegian Passport
from Mr.Schaller in the German Consulate who was in charge
of the Public Investigation Department. He sent for me
about May or June 1916 and asked me to get it reproduced.
I went to the same place and was told that the work was done by
stone in Lythographie work. He said he could not do it, so I
had to find a man who specialised in stone work. I
went from one Chinaman to another until one advised me to go to
a man in Sinza Road who was a big paper merchant and a maker
of lottery tickets and such things in stone engraving. I
believe he has some Japanese assistants. I went there at
night and saw him and we made a verbal contrast for six
dollars a copy. He made 12 copies and this a photograph
of a copy (See Captain s's photo of a Norwegian passport)
I paid him $26 in advance. I got the copies, obtained the
balance of the money from Mr.Gatien, German Chancellor,-
paid the bill- and the documents I kept in my safe. I showed
them to the German Authorities - they were very satisfied.
They have them back to me to keep in my safe. They did not
want them in the Consulate. From time to time the German
Consulate sent me a photograph of a man for whom they wanted
a passport. I filled in the passport only with picture seals
and stamps. The seals and stamps I got made by the man in

英国当局签发的，另一种是由俄国当局签发的。此后，带有类似签证的护照被分发出去，照片从北京和天津寄来，护照由德国和奥地利当局在上海制作，然后送回北京、天津及其他地方。后来，德国当局认为流通中的西班牙护照太多，认为改用另一种护照并将其制作得与西班牙护照相同更为安全。他们获得了一本挪威护照。我不知道他们是如何得到的。我获得了一份原件的副本。我从德国领事馆负责公共调查部的Schaller先生那里获得了原始的挪威护照。他在1916年5月或6月左右召见我，要求我将其复制。我去了同一个地方，但被告知该项工作属于石版印刷（Lythographie）工艺，他们做不了，所以我不得不寻找一位专门从事石工的人。我询问了一个又一个中国人，直到有人建议我去新闸路（Sinza Road）找一个人，他是一位大纸商，也是彩票等物品的石版雕刻制作人。我相信他有一些日本助手。我在晚上去那里见了他，我们口头约定每份副本收费六美元。他制作了12份副本，这是其中一份副本的照片（参见s上尉拍摄的挪威护照照片）。我预付给他26美元。我拿到副本后，从德国副领事Gatien先生那里取得了余款——支付了账单——并将文件保存在我的保险箱中。我向德国当局展示了这些文件——他们非常满意。他们让我把这些文件拿回来存放在我的保险箱里。他们不想把这些文件留在领事馆。不时地，德国领事馆会寄给我一张他们希望为其办理护照的人的照片。我只需在护照上填入照片、封记和印章即可。这些封记和印章是由福州路（Foochow Road）的那个人制作的。

Foochow Road. Only four or five of these passports were
used. About the 20th of June 1916 at tiffin time Mr.Rottman
came to 43 Boone Road, a boarding house in which I was
living, looking for a man named A.Landau. We said he was
not there so he sat down at the tiffin table and introduced
himself to me and started a conversation. He at once said
he was in the British Intelligence Department and could do
marvellous things. He said he wanted his teeth fixed. In
the course of conversation he found out that I was a dentist.
He said "I will come one of these days to have my teeth fixed".
Later on two or three days after I met him in the street and
asked him why he had not come. He said,"Well, to-morrow at
5 o'clock I shall be in your office." Just prior to this
(the time I knew Rottman) a Greek came to my Office and in-
formed me that there were a number of Koreans in Shanghai who
were prepared to plot for the destruction of munitions in
Harbin and Vladivostock provided that they could induce the
German Government to announce that they would restore Korea
to the Koreans after the war. The Greek's name was A.Loverdos.
I informed him that I would inform the German Authorities of
the matter and let him know.

I went to Mr.Gatien and informed him, of my information.
He told me that I had better talk to Mr. Schaller.
and he called him downstairs to his room (this was about
the beginning of May 1916). When he came down he asked me to
go to his room upstairs as the matter interested him. I
went upstairs with him and told him roughly the story which
the Greek had told me. He told me to ask the Greek to meet
him at my office next day at 5 p.m. with the Korean. As a
matter of fact Mr.Schaller was very punctual at my Office
the following day. When he arrived the Greek and two Koreans
were there. One was an elderly man with eye-glasses and
he could only speak a certain Chinese dialect. The other
one was a better educated man and pretended to have been at

Landau的人的。我们说他不在，于是他在午餐桌旁坐下，向我自我介绍并开始交谈。他立刻声称自己在英国情报部门工作，能做出惊人的事情。他说他想修补牙齿。在谈话过程中，他发现我是一名牙医。他说：“改天我会来补牙。”后来，过了两三天，我在街上遇到他，问他为什么没来。他说：“嗯，明天5点我会去你的诊所。”就在此前不久（即我认识Rottman的时候），一名希腊人来到我的诊所，告知我上海有一些朝鲜人准备策划破坏哈尔滨和符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）的军火，前提是德国政府能宣布战后会将朝鲜归还给朝鲜人。这名希腊人名叫A. Loverdos。我告诉他，我会将此事通报德国当局，并让他知晓结果。

我去找了Gatien先生，向他通报了我所获知的信息。他告诉我，最好与Schaller先生谈谈，并把他叫到楼下的房间（这大约是1916年5月初）。Schaller先生下来后，因对此事感兴趣，请我上楼去他的房间。我随他上楼，大致讲述了那名希腊人告诉我的故事。他让我请那名希腊人第二天下午5点带那名朝鲜人到我的诊所与他见面。事实上，Schaller先生第二天非常准时地来到了我的诊所。当他到达时，那名希腊人和两名朝鲜人已经在那里。其中一人是位戴眼镜的老者，只会说某种中国方言。另一人受教育程度较高，自称曾在

the German Legation at Berlin. He spoke French fluently
and was able to write French. He also spoke a few words of
German but pretended to have forgotten it. Mr.Schaller
speaks French, Italian and English. They set out the whole
plot interpreted by the Greek who speaks Chinese and Italian.
There was an intermittent conversation in Italian, French and
Chinese between the Greek, myself,Schaller and the Koreans.
I had very little to say, I was only listening to the whole

Mr. Schaller told them that he wanted to know who the people

the stores of ammunition in Harbin and Vladivostock should

柏林的德国公使馆任职。他能流利地说法语，也能写法文。他还会说几句德语，但假装已经忘记了。Schaller先生会说法语、意大利语和英语。他们阐述了整个阴谋，由懂中文和意大利语的希腊人进行翻译。在希腊人、我、Schaller和朝鲜人之间，有意大利语、法语和中文的断续交谈。我几乎没说什么，只是在倾听整个过程。谈话的结果是，如果德国政府保证在战后协助朝鲜人收复朝鲜，这名朝鲜人和希腊人同意执行德国政府提出的任何行动。Schaller先生告诉他们，他想知道这些人是谁，那名会说法语的朝鲜人承诺向他展示自己在柏林朝鲜公使馆任职时身穿制服的照片。在会谈期间，Schaller先生暗示，德国政府更希望哈尔滨和符拉迪沃斯托克的弹药库被摧毁，从而阻止其输入欧洲。他建议他们摧毁铁路车辆工厂，并破坏铁路信号装置，这些装置是美国制造的，在俄罗斯无法获得。他还建议他们松开铁轨上的螺丝，切断电报、电话和电线，如果做到这一点，他们应尝试前往关押囚犯的营地。他承诺向他们提供高级军官的名单，以便他们与之联系，并秘密安排在某晚杀害守卫，释放囚犯，并从上海携带地图交给这些军官，以便他们能进入朝鲜领土；如果那里不够安全，则将他们带入中国领土。整个安排在一次会议中完成

我在Schaller先生的办公室，在他的助手Schobbs先生在场的情况下，从Schaller先生那里拿到了钱，并给他开了一张临时收据，同时经他同意，我从领事馆的收据簿中取出一张空白表格，目的是从希腊人那里获取收据。我回到诊所，向希腊人出示了现金，并告诉他必须填写收据，因为我需要将其出示给Schaller先生以换回我的临时收据。他照做了，我便将钱交给了他。晚上，我去了德国总会，将收据交给Schaller先生，他承诺第二天将我的临时收据还给我。但他从未兑现。我曾多次要求他还给我，但他至今未还。他说他已经销毁了它，因为对他来说已无用，他手里有希腊人的收据。在此之后，在我遇见Rottman之前，那名希腊人和朝鲜人离开了。他们离开时接到指示，所有信件均寄给史密斯夫人（Mrs. Smith），转交德国邮局。大约

14 days no letters or correspondence was received.
I asked Mr.Schaller on several occasions the reason
why no letters had been received. Mr.Schaller replied
that either they had not yet arrived or that they had
not made their arrangements perfect. After that I received
a registered letter addressed to Mrs.Smith. It said that
the Greek had some trouble in Mukden and had to return to
Peking where he had an interview with the Korean Minister,
and had so far settled matters with the Korean Minister.
Three or four days afterwards, a letter came saying that
an arrangement was made with the Korean coolies in different
villages on the railway, only that they had to be supported
with enough provisions until they would be able to obtain
provisions by means of force, and for that purpose the Greek
asked for a further advance of another $1200 or thereabouts.
When I received the letter I handed it over to Mr.Schaller as
usual. Mr.Schaller said he would consider the matter and
let me know. The next day Mr.Schaller told me he spoke
to Mr.Knipping about it, and he said that he did not think
any more money should be advanced, and to remind the Greek
and his companions that he was to get a certain percentage
of the damage done and that nothing further could be advanced
until something had been done. Before I wrote a
reply to the Greek, a telegram was received from the Greek
asking why I had not answered and requested me to show
this to the German Authorities. On the same day I wrote
to the Greek after showing his telegram to Mr.Schaller who
approved of it. The letter contained more or less what I
had been instructed to say. After 5 days later, I got a

decision of the German Authorities. I went again to Mr.
Schaller and showed him the letter and he said it would

14天内没有收到任何信件或通信。
我多次询问Schaller先生未收到信件的原因。Schaller先生回答说，要么是他们尚未抵达，要么是他们的安排尚未完善。之后，我收到了一封寄给史密斯夫人的挂号信。信中说，那名希腊人在沈阳（Mukden）遇到了一些麻烦，不得不返回北京，在那里他会见了朝鲜公使，并已就此与朝鲜公使解决了相关事宜。三四天后，又来了一封信，称已与铁路沿线不同村庄的朝鲜苦力达成了安排，只是在他们能够通过武力获取补给之前，必须为他们提供足够的物资支持，为此，希腊人要求再预支约1200美元。收到信后，我像往常一样将其交给了Schaller先生。Schaller先生说他会考虑此事并通知我。第二天，Schaller先生告诉我他与Knipping先生谈过此事，Knipping先生认为不应再预支更多款项，并要提醒希腊人及其同伴，他们将按造成破坏的一定比例获得报酬，在采取行动之前不能再预支任何款项。在我给希腊人写回信之前，收到了希腊人发来的电报，质问我为何未予回复，并要求我将此电报出示给德国当局。同日，在向批准此信的Schaller先生出示了该电报后，我给希腊人写了回信。信中内容大致是我被指示要说的话。5天后，我收到一封用法文写的信，解释为何希腊人认为1500美元不够，并要求立即电告德国当局的决定。我再次去找Schaller先生，向他出示了这封信，他说这将

want it. It was persecuted by my own Authorities, that was
why, I went over to Captain Seigne, I never was friendly
to the German or Austrian Authorities when I came to my full
sense of responsibility. All my information as a rule
went through Rottman to Captain Seigne,as I did not like
to go to his Office very often as I was afraid of being
seen by German spies. The first time I went to Captain
Seigne's house in Jessfield Road, when we came out Rottman
invited me to St.George's Farm to have a glass of beer.
When I was coming out the first person who saw me was the
Secretary of the Austrian Consulate, who did not speak to
me but gave me a suspicious look. I did not think anything
of it, but took the tramcar and went into town. I con-
tinued my duty to Captain Seigne as I had promised. The
only persons so far as I knew, who were aware of what I
was doing, were Rottman and Captain Seigne. During this
time Rottman was having his teeth fixed at my surgery, and
being an intimate friend, as I thought, I made no charges.
I continued to give information to Rottman for transmission
to Captain Seigne who paid the rent of my offices on
several occasions. On the night of the 17th or 18th of
August 1916 about 3.30a.m. I met Nielsen with a Custom's
Official named Williams or Williamson coming up in a Chinese
Lighter and carrying a big case about 1 metre high and the
same breadth. This was on the french Bund near the
Native City. I knew there was a case of ammunition
due to arrive from Hankow as I had heard it spoken of at
the German Club. Williams or Williamson was a man
who boasted that he was in receipt of a large income and
has since been dismissed from the Customs for failure of
duty. Nielsen asked me what I was doing and I said that
I was suffering from insomnia and I was just having a walk
to try and tire myself so that I could sleep. I followed

想要它。我受到我自己当局的迫害，这就是为什么我去投奔西涅上尉的原因。当我充分意识到自己的责任时，我对德国或奥地利当局从未友好过。通常情况下，我所有的情报都通过罗特曼转交给西涅上尉，因为我不喜欢经常去他的办公室，生怕被德国间谍看见。我第一次去西涅上尉位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的寓所，当我们出来时，罗特曼邀请我去圣乔治农场（St. George's Farm）喝一杯啤酒。当我出来时，第一个看见我的是奥地利领事馆秘书，他没有和我说话，只是怀疑地看了我一眼。我没把这当回事，而是乘电车进了市区。我继续履行对西涅上尉的承诺。据我所知，唯一知道我在做什么的人是罗特曼和西涅上尉。在此期间，罗特曼在我的诊所治牙，鉴于我认为他是密友，我没有收费。我继续向罗特曼提供情报，由他转交给西涅上尉，后者曾几次支付我办公室的租金。1916年8月17日或18日凌晨3点30分左右，我遇见尼尔森和一名名叫威廉斯（Williams）或威廉姆森（Williamson）的海关官员，他们坐着一艘中式舢板上来，抬着一个大约1米高、同样宽的大箱子。地点在法外滩靠近老城厢处。我知道有一箱弹药将从汉口运抵，因为我曾在德国俱乐部听到人们谈论此事。威廉斯或威廉姆森是一个吹嘘自己收入丰厚的人，后来因失职被海关开除。尼尔森问我在做什么，我说我患有失眠症，正在散步以试图让自己疲惫从而入睡。我跟随

them as close as possible to try and find out where they
were taking the box. They had two coolies to carry
the box. They put it in a hand cart. I found that the
box was taken to Jinkee Road to the back door of the German
Club, where a man whom I suspected to a Mr. From
took delivery of the box and took it into the Club. I
went home as I did not want to be seen again. I did
not communicate this to Captain Seigne at once as I did
not want to say anything until I had a complete story.
The next day was the 18th of August when the Austrian and
German Consulates were closed on account of the late
Emperor's birthday. On that day I happened to meet Nielsen
and Williamson at Neuman's Bar about 11.30 a.m. I did
not speak to them. I had a glass of beer and walked out.
The next day about 9.30a.m. a telephone message came to Dr.
Cox's house, let to a Mrs.Steinberg, where I was staying,
that I should go to the office immediately as the Secretary
of the Austrian Consulate wanted to see me. I went at
once to the office where I met the Secretary at the door.
He told me the Consul-General wanted to see me. I asked
him why and he said he did not know as it might be a private
affair between myself and the Consul-General. When I went
to the Consulate I had to wait five or ten minutes. I noticed
that everybody looked at me with suspicion. I did not sus-
pect that anybody had given me away. About 10 minutes
later I was brought into the Vice Consul's room where
the Imperial Chancellor of the German Consulate was, Leon
Max Schaller, with his assistant Mr.Schopp and the Austrian
Vice Consul Mr.A.Kunz. They asked me if I knew why I was
there and I said no. They said I was there for breaking
certain paragraphs of the law and told me the number which
I do not remember. I asked them for an explanation of the
meaning of the paragraph and they said that the meaning of

他们尽可能近，试图查明他们要把箱子带到哪里去。他们有两个苦力搬运箱子。他们把箱子放在一辆手推车上。我发现箱子被带到了静安寺路（Jinkee Road）德国俱乐部的后门，一个我怀疑是弗罗姆（From）先生的人接收了箱子并将其带入俱乐部。我回家了，因为我不想再次被人看见。我没有立即将此情况通报给西涅上尉，因为我想在掌握完整情况之前不发表任何意见。第二天是8月18日，奥地利和德国领事馆因已故皇帝诞辰而关闭。那天上午11点30分左右，我碰巧在纽曼酒吧（Neuman's Bar）遇见了尼尔森和威廉姆森。我没有和他们说话。我喝了一杯啤酒就走了。第二天上午9点30分左右，我借住的考克斯（Cox）博士寓所（租给斯坦伯格（Steinberg）夫人）接到电话，让我立即去办公室，因为奥地利领事馆秘书要见我。我立刻去了办公室，在门口见到了秘书。他告诉我总领事要见我。我问为什么，他说他不知道，因为这可能是我和总领事之间的私事。当我到达领事馆时，不得不等了五到十分钟。我注意到每个人都用怀疑的眼光看着我。我并不怀疑有人出卖了我。大约10分钟后，我被带进副领事的房间，德国领事馆的帝国 Chancellor（原文如此，指高级官员）莱昂·马克斯·沙勒（Leon Max Schaller）及其助手肖普（Schopp）先生，以及奥地利副领事A.昆兹（A. Kunz）先生都在那里。他们问我是否知道为何在此，我说不知道。他们说我来此是因为违反了某些法律条款，并告诉了我条款编号，但我记不清了。我要求解释该条款的含义，他们说该条款的意思是

pages.en:
14
the paragraph was that being entrusted with Government money
I had converted it to my own use. They had the re-
ceipt and correspondence which proved clearly that I had
handed over the money to the Greek. The Vice Consul
walked out, came back in about 5 minutes and said that I
had been arrested. I protested against it and the Consul
General was then called in. He said that there were other
charges against me which they had to enquire into. Outside
were waiting two German Detectives (Deitrich & Helmert).
In the meantime a Motor Car was called and the two detectives
the Vice Consul, the Secretary Mr. Schalles, Mr.
Schopp his assistant and myself went to my surgery at 34
Nanking Road where all my papers were searched and all blank
passports stamps etc were seized. The passports and stamps
were Hidden so that the German Detectives could not
see them. After they had made a thorough search the papers
were tied up in a towel or newspaper and after that they took
me to my residence, 39 North Soochow Road and further searched
there finding nothing of importance. After that only the
two German detectives and the Secretary of the Austrian
Consulate drove me in the same car to the French Bund and
the matter was only a matter of a few days and that any
citizen could be arrested on suspicion. I was put on
board a sampan and taken to the German steamer "Heida" and
handed over there to two other detectives who were in charge
of several prisoners. I was not allowed to talk to any-
body. I was kept on board and watched by two detectives
Bierbaum and Baumok. Rumours were spread in town that I
had committed suicide. Many different ways were mentioned,
some said I had drowned myself, some that I had shot my-
self, and another that I had been shot by a detective.
Rumours were so prevalent that the German Consulate sent on
board the steamer Inspector Helmert to ascertain the truth.

既然受托管理政府资金，我却将其挪作私用。他们持有收据和往来信件，清楚地证明我已将钱款交给那个希腊人。副领事走了出去，大约5分钟后回来说，我被捕了。我提出抗议，随后总领事被叫来。他说对我还有其他指控需要调查。外面等着两名德国侦探（迪特里希 Deitrich 和赫尔默特 Helmert）。与此同时，叫来了一辆汽车，两名侦探、副领事、秘书沙勒斯（Schalles）先生、他的助手肖普先生和我一同前往南京路34号我的诊所，那里所有的文件都被搜查，所有空白护照、印章等都被没收。护照和印章被藏了起来，以免被德国侦探发现。在彻底搜查后，文件被包在毛巾或报纸里，随后他们带我去了苏州河北路39号我的住所，并在那里进一步搜查，未发现重要物品。之后，只有两名德国侦探和奥地利领事馆秘书同车将我送到法外滩，并表示这不过是几天的事，任何公民都可以因涉嫌被捕。我被送上一艘舢板，带到德国轮船“海达号”（Heida）上，并在那里移交给另外两名负责看守几名囚犯的侦探。我不被允许与任何人交谈。我被关在船上，由两名侦探比尔鲍姆（Bierbaum）和鲍莫克（Baumok）监视。城里流传着我自杀的谣言。说法各异，有人说我投水自尽，有人说我开枪自杀，还有人说我被一名侦探枪杀。谣言如此盛行，以至于德国领事馆派遣赫尔默特巡官登上轮船以查明真相。

15

When I was in custody my wife was called nearly every day
to the German Consulate and asked different questions, and
she said she did not know anything I did, as I never dis-
closed any of my affairs to her. She said on several
occasions Ettinger was very busy at the Austrian Consulate
producing witnesses against me which were not competent, and
after 3 weeks, about the 7th of September, I was released
by the Austrian Authorities upon the condition that I would
not leave Shanghai without their knowledge and would not
speak or take revenge of any kind against both Governments,
and on taking that oath I was released. I asked them
to publish in the papers the fact that I was innocently
arrested so that I could get back my character.
They refused to do that and said that if the German
and Austrian community saw me at liberty they would under-
stand that I was not guilty of any offence whatever.
Wanting to communicate with Captain Seigne, I went to Mr.
Boyes of Boyes & Masset and asked him to telephone to Captain
Seigne stating I wanted to see him. He did so, and Captain
Seigne came to see me at Boyes & Massett's premises, Captain
Seigne said he was glad to see me out of trouble and I ex-
plained to him more or less why I was arrested. Captain
Seigne asked me about my financial condition and promised to
send me Tls.200, which he did. As I was always in touch
with Japanese Ammunition brokers two or three days after my
release a Japanese broker came to me and asked if I knew any-
who wanted to buy ammunition. I said "Yes" and made an
appointment with him at 7.30 or 8.00 in the evening. In
the meantime I told Captain Seigne about it through Mr. Boyes
and so far as I know Captain Seigne communicated with Captain
Hilton Johnson and as a matter of fact in the afternoon a
Municipal Detective came to me and in the presence of Mr.
Boyes made arrangements with me to call at 7.30 or 8 o'clock

15

在我被拘留期间，我的妻子几乎每天都被叫到德国领事馆接受各种询问，她说她对我的所作所为一无所知，因为我从未向她透露过我的任何事务。她多次提到，埃廷格（Ettinger）在奥地利领事馆忙于制造针对我的证人证言，但这些证人并不具备资格。三周后，大约在9月7日，奥地利当局释放了我，条件是我未经他们许可不得离开上海，并且不得对两国政府发表任何言论或进行任何形式的报复。在宣誓遵守上述条件后，我获释。我要求他们在报纸上刊登我无辜被捕的事实，以便恢复我的名誉。他们拒绝这样做，并称如果德奥社群看到我获得自由，就会明白我没有任何罪行。为了与西涅上尉联系，我找到博伊斯和马塞特公司（Boyes & Masset）的博伊斯（Boyes）先生，请他打电话给西涅上尉，说我想见他。他照办了，西涅上尉来到博伊斯和马塞特公司的办公地点见我。西涅上尉表示很高兴看到我摆脱困境，我向他大致解释了被捕的原因。西涅上尉询问了我的财务状况，并承诺寄给我200两银子，他也确实这样做了。由于我一直与日本军火经纪人保持联系，在我获释两三天后，一名日本经纪人来找我，问我是否认识想买弹药的人。我说“认识”，并与他约定当晚7点30分或8点见面。与此同时，我通过博伊斯先生将此事告知了西涅上尉，据我所知，西涅上尉与希尔顿·约翰逊（Hilton Johnson）上尉进行了联系，事实上，当天下午一名公共租界侦探来找我，在博伊斯先生在场的情况下，与我安排好在晚上7点30分或8点

pages.en:
16

in the evening at my house No.39 North Soochow Road where
I was expecting a Japanese broker. The Japanese Broker
came and I went with him and a Detective followed us to
Helen Terrace North Szechun Road Extension where I was intro-
duced to the supposed Japanese owner. It took over half an
hour to make arrangements with them. They told me the
ammunition was not there but in Nanzing Road. When I came
out I did not see the Detective. I went with the Japanese
where I convinced myself of the existence of the ammunition.
I then went back to Helen Terrace to find the detective but
could not see him anywhere. I had promised to bring the buyer
at 10 p.m. I went to the North Szechun Road Police Station
where I enquired about the Detective. The Sergeant on
duty a thin person with a lame leg pretended to know all about
it and I told him I wished to see the detective. I do not
remember his name. He rang him up on the phone and I gave
him all necessary instructions. The Police made a raid
on the house about 10.30 the same evening in Nanzing Road
just behind Ettinger's house. The raid was carried out
so badly that the Japanese had time to remove most of the
ammunition and the Police only found a few Brownings and
some ammunition, this I heard the next day. One or two
Japanese were charged for being unlawfully in possession
of arms, one I believe got two months. The next day a
Japanese woman went to my Consul and reported to him that
I was working for the British Authorities, and told him
what had happened the previous evening. As a matter of
fact the public were warned in the Japanese papers that a
man of the name of Max Kindler was a British Government
spy. My Consul called me and asked me about it and told me
that a woman had come to him complaining about me and gave me
to understand that he knew everything about my doings and there
was not a single thing which I had done or will do that was
not known to him. I denied everything and asked him

16

到我位于苏州河北路39号的家中，我当时正等待一名日本经纪人。日本经纪人来了，我随他同行，一名侦探跟随我们到了北四川路延伸段的海伦公寓（Helen Terrace），在那里我被介绍给所谓的日本货主。与他们达成协议花了半个多小时。他们告诉我弹药不在那里，而在南京路。出来时，我没看见那名侦探。我随日本人而去，在那里我确认了弹药的存在。随后我回到海伦公寓寻找那名侦探，但到处都找不到他。我曾答应在晚上10点带买家来。我去了北四川路警察局，询问那名侦探的情况。值班警长是个瘦子，腿有点瘸，假装对此事全知全能，我告诉他我想见那名侦探。我不记得他的名字了。他用电话联系了那名侦探，我给出了所有必要的指示。警方于当晚10点30分左右突袭了南京路的一处房屋，就在埃廷格家后面。这次突袭执行得非常糟糕，日本人有时机转移大部分弹药，警方只查获了几支勃朗宁手枪和一些弹药，这是我第二天听说的。一两名日本人因非法持有武器被起诉，我相信其中一人被判两个月监禁。第二天，一名日本女子去见我的领事，向他报告我为英国当局工作，并告诉他前一天晚上发生的事。事实上，日本报纸警告公众，一个叫马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）的人是英国政府间谍。我的领事召见我并询问此事，告诉我有一名女子来向他投诉我，并让我明白他知道我的一切行为，我所做或将做的每一件事他都知晓。我否认了一切，并问他

pages.en:
17
for proof and he said that the day would come when he would
have proof in his hands. I replied that when he got that
he could punish me. I then left. I found out later that
the Japanese woman was one kept by a man named Kopplin a
German subject. I believe he is no longer protected by
the German Consulate. I informed Captain Seigne about every-
thing that had happened and I continued my best to obtain
information for Captain Seigne. As the Austrian and German
Community were suspicious of me it was very difficult for me to
find out anything. One day when I came into the Club
the Secretary of the Austrian Consulate informed me that
several members objected to me and that I had better stay
away. As Rottman saw that I could not give any more
information to Captain Seigne he approached me about January
of this year and asked me to confirm everything he said,
in fact he asked me to put a story together as follows:-
"That their exists a system of basis for submarines and
other hostile bases in Batavia." He asked me to say that
I had heard this. He told me a great deal more but
I cannot remember all he said. I said I would not do so.
He told me he was my superior and if I did not do so he would
try and get me out of Captain Seigne's good graces. He
said if I listened to him and did as he told me he could
obtain more money and I could still remain on the same
good terms with Captain Seigne. I repeated that I could
not do it. I then informed Captain Seigne about it.
I also told Mrs Boyes that Rottman wanted me to repeat
stories which I did not and could not repeat. After that
Rottman got angry with me and tried to do me every possible
harm. As a matter of fact in the Savoy Hotel (about
February) I went into one room where I thought I could get
information for Captain Seigne, and as I came into the
room I found Rottman. When I went in he went out. After
about 5 minutes he came back and in the presence of 4 or 5
gentlemen he made statements showing me to be one of the

作为证据，他说总有一天他会把证据掌握在手中。我回答说，等他拿到证据后，他可以惩罚我。随后我便离开了。后来我得知，那名日本女子是由一名名为科普林（Kopplin）的德国籍男子包养的。我相信他已不再受德国领事馆的保护。我将发生的一切告知了塞涅（Seigne）上尉，并继续尽力为塞涅上尉获取情报。由于奥地利和德国侨民社群对我心存疑虑，我很难打听到任何消息。有一天，当我进入俱乐部时，奥地利领事馆秘书通知我，有几名成员对我表示反对，我最好回避。由于罗特曼（Rottman）看出我无法再向塞涅上尉提供更多信息，他在今年一月左右接近我，要求我证实他所说的一切，实际上他是要求我编造如下故事：“在巴达维亚存在一个潜艇基地及其他敌对基地的基础体系。”他要求我声称我曾听说过此事。他还告诉了我许多其他事情，但我已记不清全部内容。我说我不会这样做。他说他是我的上级，如果我不照做，他会设法让我失去塞涅上尉的信任。他说，如果我听他的话并按他的吩咐去做，他能弄到更多的钱，而我仍可与塞涅上尉保持良好的关系。我再次表示我不能这样做。随后我将此事告知了塞涅上尉。我还告诉博伊斯（Boyes）夫人，罗特曼想让我复述那些我并未听说且无法复述的故事。此后，罗特曼对我勃然大怒，并试图尽一切可能伤害我。事实上，在萨伏伊酒店（Savoy Hotel）（大约在二月），我走进一个房间，以为可以从那里为塞涅上尉获取情报，当我进入房间时，发现了罗特曼。我进去时，他便出去了。大约5分钟后，他回来了，并在四五位绅士面前发表言论，将我描绘成

pages.en:
18

worst characters in the world. He said I took money from
Captain Seigne, that I was a British Spy, he could prove
it by the cheques he cashed for me and other matters of a
similar nature. The people I was with were Russian and Turks
known to Ettinger. I did not reply, I waited for a while
and Rottman went out. The persons there told him
that as he had spoken to let me say something, then Rottman
went out. I went to Captain Seigne and told him about
this. The same evening two Austrians came to me at
my office and told me to be careful as I was playing with
fire and if the Austrian Authorities listened to what
Rottman had told them I would get into a Hell of a fix.
I begged them not to say anything more and I denied
everything. One day after this I found out that there
was a wireless on the Austrian steamers. I told this
to Captain Seigne and as I was coming out of Captain
Seigne's office I saw Rottman speaking to a man with a
beard, he (Rottman) was very angry with me and called me
names. I reported the incident to Captain Seigne later
and he told me it was alright. I have not spoken to
Rottman for about 5 months. I heard about Ettinger's
arrest about the first or second of June. I happened to
be walking in Yangtsepoo about 5.30 or 6 p.m. and was
stopped by a lady who asked me if I was Mr.Kindler.
She told me to be careful as Rottman had told her that he
would injure me in any way he could.

世界上最恶劣的人物之一。他说我从塞涅上尉那里拿钱，说我是英国间谍，他可以通过为我兑现的支票以及其他类似事项来证明这一点。当时与我在一起的人是埃廷格（Ettinger）认识的俄罗斯人和土耳其人。我没有回应，我等了一会儿，罗特曼便出去了。在场的人告诉他，既然他已经说了话，就让我说几句，然后罗特曼便出去了。我去找塞涅上尉，将此事告诉了他。当晚，两名奥地利人来到我的办公室，叫我小心行事，说我这是在玩火，如果奥地利当局听信罗特曼对他们说的话，我会陷入极大的麻烦。我恳求他们不要再说什么，并否认了一切。在此之后的一天，我发现奥地利轮船上装有无线电设备。我将此事告诉了塞涅上尉，当我从塞涅上尉的办公室出来时，看见罗特曼正在与一名留胡子的男子交谈，他（罗特曼）对我非常愤怒，并对我恶语相向。后来我向塞涅上尉报告了这一事件，他说没关系。我已经大约有5个月没有和罗特曼说过话了。我是在六月一日或二日左右听说埃廷格被捕的消息的。当时我碰巧在下午五点半或六点左右走在杨树浦（Yangtsepoo），被一位女士拦住，她问我是否是金德勒（Kindler）先生。她叫我小心，因为罗特曼曾告诉她，他会尽其所能伤害我。

I. O. R. E.
No. 1265
28/6/17.

Statement of Max Kindler, 8th June 1917.

I am a Dentist residing lately at 34 Nanking Road,
(above Boyes Basset & Co). I sold my office two months
ago to Dr. Cameron, since when I have been residing at 63
Broadway Terrace, but for the last two days at the French
Hotel.

I was born in Braila in Roumania in 1886, my father being
Austrian and my mother Dutch. I was educated in Vienna and
Berlin. I took my Dental Degrees in Berlin. After I got
my degrees I practiced in Vienna as an Assistant in 1906
for 8 months. From Vienna I went to Bucharest. I remained
in Bucharest for 13 or 14 months during the Exposition. In
Bucharest I was a Dental Surgeon assisting Dr. Lempard (Dentist
de la Court Royal). From Bucharest I travelled for about 8
months through the Holy Land, Turkey, Greece and Egypt. I
settled in Egypt (1908) where I was first an assistant to Dr.
Bacer in Alexandria. After some time I became acquainted
with Lt. Col. Maxwell, R.A.M.C. and through his influence I
became a Dental Surgeon in the Mustapha Pasha Barracks Ramlie
Alexandria. I was there for over a year. After that I went
to Madras, India. This was in November 1911. In Madras I
became Dental Surgeon to General Hospital in Madras, my
superior being Major Badcock R.A.M.C. I remained in this
employ for about 4 or 5 months and then I established myself
at Montrode, Madras. Major Badcock was displeased at my
leaving and only gave me a certificate "for a few weeks". I
remained in Madras until 1913 when I sold my goodwill to a
Dr. Halar for R. 2000. From there I returned to Egypt, in
February 1913 where I was seeking employment but could not
get a suitable position. In the beginning of 1914 I bought
a whole Dental outfit at Alexandria (receipts produced).
I remained the whole time in either Alexandria or Cairo.
In the beginning of 1914 I went to Singapore and established
myself in Battery Road, Macalisters Building. I had spent

1917年6月28日。

马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）陈述，1917年6月8日。

我是一名牙医，最近居住在南京路34号，
（博伊斯·巴塞特公司（Boyes Basset & Co）楼上）。两个月前，我将诊所卖给了卡梅伦（Cameron）医生，此后我一直居住在百老汇大厦（Broadway Terrace）63号，但最近两天住在法兰西饭店（French Hotel）。

我于1886年出生在罗马尼亚的布勒伊拉（Braila），父亲是奥地利人，母亲是荷兰人。我在维也纳和柏林接受教育。我在柏林获得了牙科学位。获得学位后，我于1906年在维也纳作为一名助手执业了8个月。从维也纳我去了布加勒斯特。在博览会期间，我在布加勒斯特停留了13或14个月。在布加勒斯特，我担任牙科外科医生，协助兰帕德（Lempard）医生（皇家宫廷牙医）。离开布加勒斯特后，我花了大约8个月时间游历圣地、土耳其、希腊和埃及。我定居在埃及（1908年），起初在亚历山大港担任巴瑟尔（Bacer）医生的助手。一段时间后，我结识了皇家陆军医疗队（R.A.M.C.）的麦克斯韦（Maxwell）中校，并通过他的影响，我成为亚历山大港拉姆利（Ramlie）穆斯塔法帕夏军营（Mustapha Pasha Barracks）的牙科外科医生。我在那里待了一年多。之后我去了印度马德拉斯。那是1911年11月。在马德拉斯，我成为马德拉斯总医院的牙科外科医生，我的上级是皇家陆军医疗队的巴德科克（Badcock）少校。我受雇于此约4或5个月，随后在马德拉斯的蒙特罗德（Montrode）自立门户。巴德科克少校对我的离职感到不满，只给我开具了一份“为期几周”的证明。我留在马德拉斯直到1913年，当时我将商誉以2000卢比的价格卖给了一位哈拉尔（Halar）医生。从那里我于1913年2月返回埃及，在那里寻找工作，但未能找到合适的职位。1914年初，我在亚历山大港购买了一整套牙科设备（已出示收据）。
在此期间，我一直待在亚历山大港或开罗。1914年初，我前往新加坡，并在麦克阿里斯特大楼（Macalisters Building）的电池路（Battery Road）自立门户。我已花费

pages.en:
2
the most of my money in establishing myself, and when war
broke out I had no means to leave Singapore, so I became ac-
quainted with a man named H.Schratter an Austrian Subject at
the Van Wijk Hotel. This man proposed to advance me enough
money to establish myself in Shanghai and pay my passage if
I would take him in as a partner. I agreed to this, and left
Singapore by a P & O Steamer. I obtained my ticket by pro-
ducing a card of my brother's, a Roumanian Subject who occupied
a position in Singapore. I arrived in Shanghai in the early
part of September 1914. I stayed at the Grand Hotel.
A few days after I arrived, I went to the Austrian Consulate,
and explained that I wished to establish myself as a Dutch
Surgeon with my partner. I had not enough documents to es-
tablish my nationality and on the assurance of two bona fide
witnesses, Schratter and his nephew, he registered me. I
started in business at 34 Nanking Road in the middle of Sep-
tember. At the end of November and the beginning of December
I came to know that my partner was a man of very bad character.
This was told me by several of my patients. I then went to
my Consul and asked him to get a dissolution of partnership,
and on the 28th of December I paid Schratter Tls.1000 to
dissolve the partnership; this was the amount he advanced.
I had to borrow this money from different parties. Since
that time I have been by myself. At the end of March 1915
the Chinaman from whom I purchased the furniture on an in-
stalment basis began to give me trouble. I went to my
Consul who ordered me to return the furniture within four
hours upon payment of the amount already paid less 10%
for wear and tear. I then went to an auction shop in
Kiangso Road. It was carried on by Ettinger. I pur-
chased some furniture for $395. This was the first time
I had met Ettinger. After being convinced that the furniture
pages.zh:
2
大部分资金用于自立门户，当战争爆发时，我没有资金离开新加坡，因此我在范维克酒店（Van Wijk Hotel）结识了一名名为H.施拉特（H.Schratter）的奥地利籍男子。此人提议预支足够的资金供我在上海立足，并支付我的旅费，条件是我接纳他为合伙人。我同意了这一提议，并乘坐半岛及东方轮船公司（P & O）的轮船离开新加坡。我通过出示我哥哥的名片获得了船票，我哥哥是罗马尼亚籍，在新加坡任职。我于1914年9月初抵达上海。我住在大华饭店（Grand Hotel）。
抵达几天后，我去了奥地利领事馆，解释说我希望与我的合伙人一起以荷兰外科医生的身份开业。我没有足够的文件来证明我的国籍，但在两位可信证人——施拉特及其侄子——的保证下，他为我进行了注册。我于9月中旬在南京路34号开始营业。11月底至12月初，我得知我的合伙人人品极差。这是我的几位病人告诉我的。于是我去找我的领事，请求他解除合伙关系，并于12月28日支付给施拉特1000两白银以解除合伙关系；这是他预支的金额。
我不得不向各方借这笔钱。自那时起，我便独自经营。1915年3月底，那位我以分期付款方式向其购买家具的中国人开始给我制造麻烦。我去找我的领事，他命令我在四小时内归还家具，条件是退还已付金额，扣除10%作为磨损费。随后我去了江苏路（Kiangso Road）的一家拍卖行。该行由埃廷格（Ettinger）经营。我以395美元的价格购买了一些家具。这是我第一次见到埃廷格。在确信交付给我的家具

pages.en:
3
which was delivered to me was not what I had bought, I had
an argument with Ettinger. Since that time I had never
spoken to him. About 3 or 4 months later I heard that
Ettinger was in the employ of the German Consulate as a
secret service man. I heard that he was under Dr. Vorenssoh
and was making Russian subjects, German protected subjects,
for payment. This was well known to the Police Authorities.
One day in the beginning of 1916 I was shown a Russian pass-
port, the filled-in portion of which had been washed with
acid so that it could be filled in by any person. This was
shown to me by a German client. He did not give me his real
name, and the passport was written in Russian, which language
I am unable to read. He asked my opinion about it. I saw
immediately that it was a washed passport, as the paper was
slightly damaged and the ink was fresh. I warned him, and
told him that it was too dangerous to run the risk, so he
went to the German Authorities and told them that it was too
dangerous for him to travel on that passport as it could be
clearly seen that it was forged. They asked him who had
told him that, and asked why he did not detect that when it
was given to him. Being an officer, he had to confess that
I had told him. I was then called to the German Chancellor
(Gatien) and he asked me for an explanation as to how I had
detected the forgery. I said that it was very poorly
done, and that if they could not do anything better than that
they should not put a person in a position of such risk.
He then asked me what they could do, as they had different
officers in Shanghai, Tientsin and Peking who had to be sent
home, some of whom had escaped from Siberian Camps; so I
told him to find original neutral passports and to print them
in Shanghai and work them out properly so as to make it im-
possible to detect a forgery. I then left. About a
pages.zh:
3
并非我所购买的那些后，我与埃廷格发生了争执。自那时起，我再也没有和他说过话。大约3或4个月后，我听说埃廷格受雇于德国领事馆，担任秘密特工。我听说他受沃伦索赫（Vorenssoh）博士领导，并通过收费将俄罗斯籍人士变为受德国保护的人士。警方当局对此十分清楚。1916年初的一天，有人向我展示了一本俄罗斯护照，其填写部分已被酸液洗去，以便任何人重新填写。这是一位德国客户向我展示的。他没有告诉我他的真实姓名，而且护照是用俄文写的，这种语言我无法阅读。他征求我的意见。我立刻看出那是一本被清洗过的护照，因为纸张略有损坏，且墨迹很新。我警告了他，并告诉他冒这个风险太危险，于是他去找德国当局，告诉他们使用那本护照旅行太危险，因为可以清楚地看出它是伪造的。他们问他谁告诉他的，并问他为什么在拿到护照时没有察觉。作为一名军官，他不得不承认是我告诉他的。随后我被召见至德国领事（加蒂安（Gatien）），他要求我解释是如何识破伪造的。我说做得非常拙劣，如果他们不能做得比这更好，就不应将人置于如此大的风险之中。然后他问他们该怎么办，因为他们在上海、天津和北京有不同的官员需要送回国，其中一些人是从西伯利亚营地逃出来的；于是我建议他们寻找原始的 neutral（中立国）护照，在上海进行印刷并妥善制作，使其无法被识破为伪造品。随后我便离开了。大约

pages.en:
4
fortnight later an Officer came to me but did not give me his
proper name. He said he lived at the German Club and begged
me to assist him as he was sent by the German Authorities.
He asked me to procure for him a good passport. A few
days before that, a loafer came to beg and I asked him what
nationality he was, and he said he was a Roumanian. I asked
for his documents and he showed me a Spanish Passport on
which was written:- "Il Consul General de Espana at Shanghai".
This was the top line and on the next line:- "Il Regnio de
Romanes in Esta". The passport was in the name of Kobaks.
I returned this document to him and gave him 40 cts. I did
not see him until later, after my interview with the German
Officer, when I saw him in the Public Gardens. He came
to me again and I asked him where he was living and he told
me in some Chinese hotel. I asked him where I could find
him in case I needed him and he told me at a Chinese barber's
shop in the Tientsing Road. Late one afternoon about 4.30
the Officer came again and said that I must do my best to
get him a passport. I took him to the Public Gardens and
looked for the man but I could not find him anywhere till I
heard he was working in the Casual Ward. I went the same
evening with this officer to the Casual Ward where I met
a Mr. Harris. He received us in his drawing room and offered
us a drink. I asked him if there was a man of the name of
Kobaks in his ward, he asked us why we wanted him and we
said we had a job for him and he must leave to-night. He
said if I could be sure that Kobaks would have somewhere
to sleep, he would let him out. We gave him our assurance
that the man would be in good hands, and on account of
that Mr. Harris gave the man over to our charge. We
took the man and when we got into the street
pages.zh:
4
两周后，一名军官来找我，但没有告诉我他的真实姓名。他说他住在德国俱乐部，并恳求我帮助他，因为他是德国当局派来的。他要求我为他搞到一本好的护照。在那之前几天，有一个流浪汉来乞讨，我问他是什么国籍，他说他是罗马尼亚人。我要求看他的证件，他给我看了一本西班牙护照，上面写着：“Il Consul General de Espana at Shanghai”（西班牙驻上海总领事）。这是第一行，下一行写着：“Il Regnio de Romanes in Esta”。护照上的名字是科巴克斯（Kobaks）。我将这份文件还给了他，并给了他40分。直到后来，在我与德国军官面谈之后，我在公共花园（Public Gardens）再次见到他时，我才又见到他。他又来找我，我问他住在哪里，他说住在某家中国旅馆。我问他如果需要找他可以在哪里找到他，他说在天津路（Tientsing Road）的一家中国理发店。某天下午大约四点半，那名军官又来了，说我必须尽力为他搞到一本护照。我带他去公共花园寻找那个人，但到处都找不到，直到听说他在临时收容所（Casual Ward）工作。当晚我和这名军官一起去了临时收容所，在那里我们见到了哈里斯（Harris）先生。他在客厅接待了我们，并请我们喝酒。我问他收容所里是否有一个名叫科巴克斯的人，他问我们要找他做什么，我们说我们有份工作给他，他必须今晚离开。他说如果我能确保科巴克斯有地方睡觉，他就放他出去。我们向他保证这个人会得到妥善照顾，因此哈里斯先生将这个人交给我们照管。我们带走了那个人，当我们走到街上

pages.en:
5
I asked him if he had his passport with him, and
he said No. I then asked him where it was and he said he
had left it in the Ward with his clothes. He returned
immediately to the Ward, and after about 10 minutes brought
his clothes with the passport. I handed over the passport
to the officer and we took Kobaka to the Tollefsen Hotel,
where we paid for his board and lodging for the time being.
As we had had no dinner, the officer invited me to Mouran's
Restaurant where he we had dinner. The following day the officer
came in the morning and asked me if I had said anything about
printing to the German Authorities, and asked if this passport
could not be printed. I told him that unless the German
Consulate agreed to it, I would not do it. As I had seen with
my own eyes at C.Berthel's Office a similar passport (Russian)
also forged with the stamp, seal and signature in perfect
condition, which was a very good forgery, I thought the same
could be done with the Spanish passport. The officer went
away and took the passport with him. In the afternoon I was
called to the German Consulate when I was told that it was
quite safe and that I may do it for the man. The Officer
then told me that I could have it done for him and to go to
a printer and he would pay all the expenses. I went to a
printer who carries on business opposite the Central Police
Station and he made all the paper stamps. It took him
4 or 5 days to do it. I can recognise the photograph which
was forged if I see it. I got back the original passport
filled in one blank pass with a typewriter as the original
was, and returned the original to Kobaka for the use of his
passport. The officer gave Kobaka $50 and paid his Hotel
Bill and paid my expenses which were about $26. This took
place in the early part of 1918 about March. At the same
time Mr.Berthel an Austrian, used to furnish the German
Authorities with forgeries of two visas, one made by the
pages.zh:

我问他是否随身携带护照，他说没有。接着我问他护照在哪里，他说他把护照和衣服一起留在了病房里。他立即返回病房，大约10分钟后带着衣服和护照回来了。我将护照交给警官，随后我们将Kobaka带到托勒夫森旅馆（Tollefsen Hotel），并暂时为他支付了食宿费用。由于我们尚未吃晚饭，警官邀请我去莫朗餐厅（Mouran's Restaurant），我们在那里用了晚餐。第二天早上，警官前来问我是否曾向德国当局提及过印刷事宜，并询问这本护照是否可以仿制印刷。我告诉他，除非德国领事馆同意，否则我不会这样做。因为我曾在C. Berthel的办公室里亲眼见过一本类似的（俄罗斯）护照，其印章、封记和签名都伪造得完好无缺，那是一次非常高明的伪造，我认为西班牙护照也可以如法炮制。警官随即离开，并带走了护照。下午，我被召至德国领事馆，被告知此事十分安全，我可以为那人办理。于是警官告诉我，可以为他办理，让我去找一家印刷商，所有费用由他支付。我找到了一位在中央巡捕房对面经营的印刷商，他制作了所有的纸质印章。这花了他4到5天的时间。如果看到那张伪造的照片，我能辨认出来。我拿回了原始护照，像原件一样用打字机填写了一张空白通行证，并将原件归还给Kobaka供其使用护照之需。警官给了Kobaka 50美元，支付了他的旅馆账单，并支付了我的费用，约为26美元。这件事发生在1918年初，大约是3月份。与此同时，奥地利人Berthel先生习惯于向德国当局提供两种签证的伪造品，一种是由

British Authorities and one by the Russian Authorities.
After that similar passports with visies were distributed
and photos were received from Peking and Tientsin and passports
were made in Shanghai by the German and Austrian Authorities
and returned to Paking and Tientsin and other places.
Afterwards the German Authorities thought that there were
too many Spanish passports in circulation, and that it was
safer to take another passport and to make it the same as
the Spanish one. They obtained a Norwegian passport.
I do not know how they got it. I obtained a copy of the
original. I obtained the original Norwegian Passport
from Mr.Schaller in the German Consulate who was in charge
of the Public Investigation Department. He sent for me
about May or June 1916 and asked me to get it reproduced.
I went to the same place and was told that the work was done by
stone in Lythographic work. He said he could not do it, so I
had to find a man who specialised in stone work. I
went from one Chinaman to another until one advised me to go to
a man in Sinza Road who was a big paper merchant and a maker
of lottery tickets and such things in stone engraving. I
believe he has some Japanese assistants. I went there at
night and saw him and we made a verbal contract for six
dollars a copy. He made 12 copies and this a photograph
of a copy (See Captain s's photo of a Norwegian passport)
I paid him $28 in advance. I got the copies, obtained the
balance of the money from Mr.Gatien, German Chancellor,-
paid the bill- and the documents I kept in my safe. I showed
them to the German Authorities they were very satisfied.
They have them back to me to keep in my safe. They did not
want them in the Consulate. From time to time the German
Consulate sent me a photograph of a man for whom they wanted
a passport. I filled in the passport only with picture seals
and stamps. The seals and stamps I got made by the man in

英国当局签发的，另一种是由俄国当局签发的。此后，带有签证的类似护照被分发出去，照片从北京和天津寄来，护照由德国和奥地利当局在上海制作，然后送回北京、天津和其他地方。后来，德国当局认为流通中的西班牙护照太多，认为换用另一种护照并将其制作得与西班牙护照相同更为安全。他们获得了一本挪威护照。我不知道他们是如何得到的。我获得了一份原件的副本。我从德国领事馆负责公共调查部的Schaller先生那里获得了原始的挪威护照。他在1916年5月或6月左右召见我，要求我将其复制。我去了同一个地方，被告知这项工作是通过石版印刷完成的。他说他做不了，所以我不得不找一个专门从事石工的人。我从一个中国人问到另一个中国人，直到有人建议我去新闸路（Sinza Road）找一个人，他是一位大纸商，也是用石刻制作彩票等物品的人。我相信他有一些日本助手。我在晚上去那里见了他，我们口头约定每份副本收费6美元。他制作了12份副本，这是其中一份副本的照片（参见s上尉拍摄的挪威护照照片）。我预付给他28美元。我拿到副本后，从德国副领事Gatien先生那里取得了余款——支付了账单——并将文件保存在我的保险箱里。我出示给德国当局看，他们非常满意。他们把文件交还给我，让我保存在保险箱里。他们不想把这些文件留在领事馆。不时地，德国领事馆会寄给我一张他们想要为其办理护照的人的照片。我只需用图片、封记和印章填写护照。这些封记和印章是由福州路的那个人制作的。

used. About the 20th of June 1918 at tiffin time Mr.Rottman
came to 43 Boone Road, a boarding house in which I was
living, looking for a man named A.Landau. He said he was
not there so he sat down at the tiffin table and introduced
himself to me and started a conversation. He at once said
he was in the British Intelligence Department and could do
marvellous things. He said he wanted his teeth fixed. In
the course of conversation he found out that I was a dentist.
He said "I will come one of these days to have my tooth fixed".
Later on two or three days after I met him in the street and
asked him why he had not come. He said,"Well, to-morrow at
5 o'clock I shall be in your office." Just prior to this
(the time I knew Rottman) a Greek came to my Office and in-
formed me that there were a number of Koreans in Shanghai who
were prepared to plot for the destruction of munitions in
Harbin and Vladivostock provided that they could induce the
German Government to announce that they would restore Korea
to the Koreans after the war. The Greek's name was A.Loverdos.
I informed him that I would inform the German Authorities of
the matter and let him know.

I went to Mr.Gation and informed him, of my information.
He told me that I had better talk to Mr. Schaller.
and he called him downstairs to his room (this was about
the beginning of May 1918). When he came down he asked me to
go to his room upstairs as the matter interested him. I
went upstairs with him and told him roughly the story which
the Greek had told me. He told me to ask the Greek to meet
him at my office next day at 5 p.m. with the Korean. As a
matter of fact Mr.Schaller was very punctual at my Office
the following day. When he arrived the Greek and two Koreans
were there. One was an elderly man with eye-glasses and
he could only speak a certain Chinese dialect. The other
one was a better educated man and pretended to have been at

Landau的人的。他说那人不在，于是他在午餐桌旁坐下，向我自我介绍并开始交谈。他立刻说他在英国情报部门工作，能做了不起的事情。他说他想修补牙齿。在谈话过程中，他发现我是一名牙医。他说：“改天我会来补牙。”后来，过了两三天，我在街上遇到他，问他为什么没来。他说：“嗯，明天5点我会去你的诊所。”就在此前不久（即我认识Rottman的时候），一名希腊人来到我的诊所，告诉我上海有一些朝鲜人准备策划破坏哈尔滨和符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）的军火，条件是他们能促使德国政府宣布战后会将朝鲜归还给朝鲜人。这名希腊人名叫A. Loverdos。我告诉他，我会将此事告知德国当局，并让他知晓结果。

我去找了Gation先生，向他通报了我所掌握的情况。他告诉我最好与Schaller先生谈谈，并把他叫到楼下的房间（这大约是1918年5月初）。当他下来时，他请我上楼去他的房间，因为此事令他感兴趣。我随他上楼，大致讲述了那名希腊人告诉我的故事。他让我请那名希腊人第二天下午5点带那名朝鲜人到我的诊所与他见面。事实上，Schaller先生第二天非常准时地来到了我的诊所。当他到达时，那名希腊人和两名朝鲜人已经在那里了。其中一人是位戴眼镜的老者，只会说某种中国方言。另一人受教育程度较高，自称曾在

8

the German Legation at Berlin. He spoke French fluently
and was able to write French. He also spoke a few words of
German but pretended to have forgotten it. Mr.Schaller
speaks French, Italian and English. They set out the whole
plot interpreted by the Greek who speaks Chinese and Italian.
There was an intermittent conversation in Italian, French and
Chinese between the Greek, myself, Schaller and the Koreans.
I had very little to say, I was only listening to the whole
thing. The result of the conversation was that the Korean
and the Greek agreed to do anything the German Government wou-
ld propose that they should do, if the German Government
would give them an assurance that they would assist them
after the war to get back Korea for the Koreans.
Mr. Schaller told them that he wanted to know who the people
were and the Korean who spoke French, promised to show him
his photo in uniform when he was employed in Berlin in the
Korean Legation. During the interview Mr.Schaller intimated
that the German Government would greatly prefer that
the stores of ammunition in Harbin and Vladivostock should
be destroyed and so prevent their import into Europe. He
suggested that they should destroy the Railway rolling Factory
and to destroy the Railway signalling apparatus, which is
American and which cannot be obtained in Russia. He also
suggested that they should open the screws on the rails,
to cut the telegraph, telephone and electric wires and if
this was done they should try and get to the camps where
the prisoners were interned. He promised to give them
the names of the Superior Officers to whom they may appeal
and make secret arrangements with them that on a certain
night they would murder the guards and release the prisoners
and take plans from Shanghai with them to hand over to the
officers so that they could come into Korean territory and
if it was not safe enough for them there, to bring them into
of the
Chinese territory. The whole arrangements were completed.

柏林的德国公使馆任职。他能流利地说法语，也能写法文。他还会说几句德语，但假装已经忘记了。Schaller先生会说法语、意大利语和英语。他们阐述了整个阴谋，由既懂中文又懂意大利语的希腊人进行翻译。在希腊人、我、Schaller和朝鲜人之间，有意大利语、法语和中文的断续交谈。我几乎没说什么，只是在倾听整个过程。谈话的结果是，如果德国政府保证在战后协助朝鲜人收回朝鲜，那名朝鲜人和希腊人同意执行德国政府提出的任何行动。Schaller先生告诉他们，他想知道这些人是谁，那名会说法语的朝鲜人答应向他展示自己在柏林朝鲜公使馆任职时身穿制服的照片。在会谈中，Schaller先生暗示，德国政府更希望哈尔滨和符拉迪沃斯托克的弹药库被摧毁，从而阻止其输入欧洲。他建议他们摧毁铁路车辆工厂，并破坏铁路信号设备，这些设备是美国制造的，在俄罗斯无法获得。他还建议他们松开铁轨上的螺丝，切断电报、电话和电线，如果做到这一点，他们应尝试前往关押囚犯的营地。他承诺向他们提供高级军官的名单，以便他们与之联系，并秘密安排他们在某个夜晚杀死守卫，释放囚犯，并从上海携带地图交给这些军官，以便他们能进入朝鲜领土；如果那里不够安全，就将他们带入中国领土。所有的安排都在一次会议中完成了。

I got the money from Mr.Schaller at his office in the
presence of Mr.Schobbs, his assistant, and gave him a
temporary receipt, and I took a blank form from the Consu-

实际上有很多次会议。完成这些安排大约花了十四天时间，最终的决定是，希腊人将获得1500美元，用于他和一名朋友以及第三名男子（一名朝鲜人）的旅费，据说这第三人此前受雇于俄国政府的铁路部门。之后，Schaller先生当着我们的面告诉希腊人，如果他来德国领事馆，就会把1500美元交给他。希腊人拒绝前往，因为他说阿斯托尔豪斯旅馆（Astor House）对面有一名英国情报部门的人员，会对进入德国领事馆的人拍照。于是我向Schaller先生建议，让他把钱带到我的诊所，亲手交给希腊人。Schaller先生说他很忙，让我去德国领事馆。星期天是我办公室里的最后一次会面。我在Schaller先生的办公室从他那里拿到了钱，当时他的助手Schobbs先生也在场，我给他开了一张临时收据，并在知会他的情况下，从领事馆的收据簿中取出一张空白表格，目的是从希腊人那里获取收据。我回到诊所，向希腊人展示了这笔钱，并告诉他必须填写收据，因为我需要把它出示给Schaller先生以换回我的临时收据。他照做了，我便将钱交给了他。晚上，我去了德国俱乐部，将收据交给Schaller先生，他承诺第二天把我的临时收据还给我。但他从未这样做。我曾多次要求他还给我，但他至今未还。他说他已经销毁了它，因为对他来说已无用，他手里有希腊人的收据。在此之后，在我遇见Rottman之前，那名希腊人和朝鲜人离开了。他们离开时接到指示，所有信件均寄给史密斯夫人（Mrs. Smith），转交德国邮局。大约有

I asked Mr.Schaller on several occasions the reason
why no letters had been received. Mr.Schaller replied
that either they had not yet arrived or that they had
not made their arrangements perfect. After that I received
a registered letter addressed to Mrs.Smith. It said that
the Greek had some trouble in Mukden and had to return to
Peking where he had an interview with the Korean Minister,
and had so far settled matters with the Korean Minister.
Three or four days afterwards, a letter came saying that
an arrangement was made with the Korean coolies in different
villages on the railway, only that they had to be supported

let me know. The next day Mr.Schaller told me he spoke

any more money should be advanced, and to remind the Greek

14天没有收到任何信件或通信。我多次询问Schaller先生未收到信件的原因。Schaller先生回答说，要么是他们尚未到达，要么是他们的安排尚未完善。之后，我收到了一封寄给史密斯夫人的挂号信。信中说，那名希腊人在沈阳（Mukden）遇到了一些麻烦，不得不返回北京，他在那里会见了朝鲜公使，并已就相关事宜与朝鲜公使达成了初步解决。三四天后，又来了一封信，称已与铁路沿线不同村庄的朝鲜苦力达成了安排，只是在他们能够通过武力获取补给之前，必须为他们提供足够的给养，为此，希腊人请求再预支约1200美元。当我收到这封信时，像往常一样交给了Schaller先生。Schaller先生说他会考虑此事并通知我。第二天，Schaller先生告诉我他与Knipping先生谈过此事，Knipper先生认为不应再预支更多款项，并要提醒希腊人及其同伴，他们将按造成破坏的一定比例获得报酬，在采取行动之前不能再预支任何款项。在我给希腊人写回信之前，收到了希腊人发来的电报，质问我为何未予回复，并要求我将此电报出示给德国当局。当天，在向批准该信的Schaller先生展示了电报后，我给希腊人写了回信。信中内容大致是我被指示要说的话。5天后，我收到一封用法文写的信，解释为何希腊人认为1500美元不够，并要求立即电告德国当局的决定。我再次去找Schaller先生，向他展示了这封信，他说这会

want it. It was persecuted by my own Authorities, that was
why, I went over to Captain Seigne, I never was friendly
to the German or Austrian Authorities when I came to my full
sense of responsibility. All my information as a rule
went through Rottman to Captain Seigne, as I did not like
to go to his Office very often as I was afraid of being
seen by German spies. The first time I went to Captain
Seigne's house in Jessfield Road, when we came out Rottman
invited me to St. George's Farm to have a glass of beer.
When I was coming out the first person who saw me was the
Secretary of the Austrian Consulate, who did not speak to
me but gave me a suspicious look. I did not think anything
of it, but took the tramcar and went into town. I con-
tinued my duty to Captain Seigne as I had promised. The
only persons so far as I knew, who were aware of what I
was doing, were Rottman and Captain Seigne. During this
time Rottman was having his teeth fixed at my surgery, and
being an intimate friend, as I thought, I made no charges.
I continued to give information to Rottman for transmission
to Captain Seigne who paid the rent of my offices on
several occasions. On the night of the 27th or 18th of
August 1916 about 3.30 a.m. I met Nielsen with a Custom's
Official named Williams or Williamson coming up in a Chinese
Lighter and carrying a big case about 1 metre high and the
same breadth. This was on the French Bund near the
Native City. ( I knew there was a case of ammunition
due to arrive from Hankow as I had heard it spoken of at
the German Club. Williams or Williamson was a man
who boasted that he was in receipt of a large income and
has since been dismissed from the Customs for failure of
duty. Nielsen asked me what I was doing and I said that
I was suffering from insomnia and I was just having a walk
to try and tire myself so that I could sleep. I followed

想要它。我受到我自己当局的迫害，这就是为什么我去投靠西格涅上尉的原因。当我充分意识到自己的责任时，我对德国或奥地利当局从未友好过。通常情况下，我所有的情报都通过罗特曼转交给西格涅上尉，因为我不喜欢经常去他的办公室，我害怕被德国间谍看到。我第一次去西格涅上尉位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的家，当我们出来时，罗特曼邀请我去圣乔治农场（St. George's Farm）喝一杯啤酒。当我出来时，第一个看到我的人是奥地利领事馆的秘书，他没有和我说话，但投来怀疑的目光。我没把这当回事，而是乘电车进了市区。我继续履行对西格涅上尉的承诺。据我所知，唯一知道我在做什么的人是罗特曼和西格涅上尉。在此期间，罗特曼在我的诊所治牙，鉴于我认为他是密友，我没有收费。我继续向罗特曼提供情报，以便转交给西格涅上尉，后者曾几次支付我办公室的租金。1916 年 8 月 27 日或 18 日晚上约凌晨 3:30，我遇到尼尔森和一名名叫威廉姆斯（Williams）或威廉姆森（Williamson）的海关官员，他们坐着一艘中式舢板上来，抬着一个大约 1 米高、同样宽的大箱子。这是在法外滩靠近老城厢的地方。（我知道有一箱弹药将从汉口运抵，因为我曾在德国俱乐部听到人们谈论此事。威廉姆斯或威廉姆森是一个吹嘘自己收入丰厚的人，后来因失职被海关开除。尼尔森问我在做什么，我说我患有失眠症，只是出来走走，试图让自己累好睡觉。我跟着

them as close as possible to try and find out where they
were taking the box. They had two coolies to carry
the box. They put it in a hand cart. I found that the
box was taken to Kinkke Road to the back door of the German
Club, where a man whom I suspected to a Mr. From
took delivery of the box and took it into the Club. I
went home as I did not want to be seen again. I did
not communicate this to Captain Seigne at once as I did
not want to say anything until I had a complete story.
The next day was the 18th of August when the Austrian and
German Consulates were closed on account of the late
Emperor's birthday. On that day I happened to meet Nielsen
and Williamson at Neuman's Bar about 11.30 a.m. I did
not speak to them. I had a glass of beer and walked out.
The next day about 8.30 a.m. a telephone message came to Dr.
Cox's house, let to a Mrs. Stenberg, where I was staying,
that I should go to the office immediately, as the Secretary
of the Austrian Consulate wanted to see me. I went at
once to the office where I met the Secretary at the door.
He told me the Consul-General wanted to see me. I asked
him why and he said he did not know as it might be a private
affair between myself and the Consul-General. When I went
to the Consulate I had to wait five or ten minutes. I noticed
that everybody looked at me with suspicion. I did not sus-
pect that anybody had given me away. About 10 minutes
later I was brought into the Vice Consul's room where
the Imperial Chancellor of the German Consulate was, Leon
Max Schaller, with his assistant Mr. Schopp and the Austrian
Vice Consul Mr. A. Kunz. They asked me if I knew why I was
there and I said no. They said I was there for breaking
certain paragraphs of the Law and told me the number which
I do not remember. I asked them for an explanation of the
meaning of the paragraph and they said that the meaning of

他们，尽可能靠近，试图找出他们要把箱子带到哪里去。他们有两个苦力搬运箱子。他们把箱子放在一辆手推车上。我发现箱子被带到了金神父路（Kingke Road，即今金陵东路附近或指某特定路段，原文拼写可能为 Kinne/Kingke）德国俱乐部的后门，一个我怀疑是弗罗姆（From）先生的人接收了箱子，并将其带入俱乐部。我回家了，因为我不想再次被人看见。我没有立即将此情况通报给西格涅上尉，因为我想在掌握完整情况之前不透露任何消息。第二天是 8 月 18 日，奥地利和德国领事馆因已故皇帝诞辰而关闭。那天上午 11:30 左右，我碰巧在纽曼酒吧（Neuman's Bar）遇到了尼尔森和威廉姆森。我没有和他们说话。我喝了一杯啤酒就走了。第二天早上 8:30 左右，有人打电话到考克斯（Cox）博士的房子——该房子租给了一位斯坦伯格（Stenberg）夫人，我当时住在那里——让我立即去办公室，因为奥地利领事馆的秘书想见我。我立刻去了办公室，在门口见到了秘书。他告诉我总领事想见我。我问为什么，他说他不知道，因为这可能是我和总领事之间的私事。当我到达领事馆时，我不得不等了五六分钟。我注意到每个人都用怀疑的眼光看着我。我没有怀疑有人出卖了我。大约 10 分钟后，我被带进副领事的房间，德国领事馆的帝国总理（Imperial Chancellor，此处指首席馆员或类似职位）莱昂·马克斯·沙勒（Leon Max Schaller）及其助手肖普（Schopp）先生，以及奥地利副领事 A. 昆兹（A. Kunz）先生都在那里。他们问我是否知道为什么来这里，我说不知道。他们说我来这里是因为违反了法律的某些条款，并告诉了我条款编号，但我记不起来了。我要求他们解释该条款的含义，他们说该条款的

the paragraph was that being entrusted with Government money
I had converted it to my own use. They had the re-
ceipt and correspondence which proved clearly that I had
handed over the money to the Greek. The Vice Consul
walked out, came back in about 5 minutes and said that I
had been arrested. I protested against it and the Consul
General was then called in. He said that there were other
charges against me which they had to enquire into. Outside
were waiting two German Detectives (Dietrich & Helmert).
In the meantime a Motor Car was called and the two detectives
the Vice Consul, the Secretary Mr. Schaller, Mr.
Schopp his assistant and myself went to my surgery at 34
Nanking Road where all my papers were searched and all blank
passports stamps etc were seized. The passports and stamps
were hidden so that the German Detectives could not
see them. After they had made a thorough search the papers
were tied up in a towel or newspaper and after that they took
me to my residence, 39 North Soochow Road and further searched
there finding nothing of importance. After that only the
two German detectives and the Secretary of the Austrian
Consulate drove me in the same car to the French Bund and
the matter was only a matter of a few days and that any
citizen could be arrested on suspicion. I was put on
board a sampan and taken to the German steamer "Heida" and
handed over there to two other detectives who were in charge
of several prisoners. I was not allowed to talk to any-
body. I was kept on board and watched by two detectives
Bierbaum and Baumok. Rumours were spread in town that I
had committed suicide. Many different ways were mentioned,
some said I had drowned myself, some that I had shot my-
self, and another that I had been shot by a detective.
Rumours were so prevalent that the German Consulate sent on
board the steamer Inspector Helmert to ascertain the truth.

含义是，我受委托管理政府资金，却将其挪作私用。他们有收据和信件，清楚地证明我已将钱交给了那个希腊人。副领事走了出去，大约 5 分钟后回来说，我被捕了。我对此提出抗议，随后总领事被叫来。他说对我还有其他指控，他们必须进行调查。外面等着两名德国侦探（迪特里希 Dietrich 和赫尔默特 Helmert）。与此同时，叫来了一辆汽车，两名侦探、副领事、秘书沙勒先生、他的助手肖普先生和我一同前往南京路 34 号我的诊所，那里所有的文件都被搜查，所有空白护照、印章等都被没收。护照和印章被藏了起来，以免被德国侦探看到。彻底搜查后，文件被包在毛巾或报纸里，之后他们带我去了苏州河北路 39 号我的住所，并在那里进行了进一步搜查，但没有发现什么重要物品。此后，只有两名德国侦探和奥地利领事馆的秘书同车将我送到法外滩，这件事仅仅过了几天，任何公民都可以因涉嫌被捕。我被送上一艘舢板，被带到德国轮船“海达号”（Heida）上，并在那里移交给另外两名负责看守几名囚犯的侦探。我不允许与任何人交谈。我被关在船上，由两名侦探比尔鲍姆（Bierbaum）和鲍莫克（Baumok）监视。城里流传着我自杀的谣言。人们议论纷纷，有人说我投水自尽，有人说我开枪自杀，还有人说我被一名侦探枪杀。谣言如此盛行，以至于德国领事馆派遣赫尔默特巡官登上轮船以查明真相。

15

When I was in custody, my wife was called nearly every day
to the German Consulate and asked different questions, and
she said she did not know anything I did, as I never dis-
closed any of my affairs to her. She said on several
occasions Ettinger was very busy at the Austrian Consulate
producing witnesses against me which were not competent, and
after 3 weeks, about the 7th of September, I was released
by the Austrian Authorities upon the condition that I would
not leave Shanghai without their knowledge and would not
speak or take revenge of any kind against both Governments,
and on taking that oath I was released. I asked them
to publish in the papers the fact that I was innocently
arrested so that I could get back my character.
They refused to do that and said that if the German
and Austrian community saw me at liberty they would under-
stand that I was not guilty of any offence whatever.
Wanting to communicate with Captain Seigne, I went to Mr.
Boyes of Boyes & Masset and asked him to telephone to Captain
Seigne stating I wanted to see him. He did so, and Captain
Seigne came to see me at Boyes & Massett's premises. Captain
Seigne said he was glad to see me out of trouble and I ex-
plained to him more or less why I was arrested. Captain
Seigne asked me about my financial condition and promised to
send me Tls.200, which he did. As I was always in touch
with Japanese Ammunition brokers two or three days after my
release a Japanese broker came to me and asked if I knew any-
who wanted to buy ammunition. I said "Yes" and made an
appointment with him at 7.30 or 8.00 in the evening. In
the meantime I told Captain Seigne about it through Mr. Boyes
and so far as I know Captain Seigne communicated with Captain
Hilton Johnson and as a matter of fact in the afternoon a
Municipal Detective came to me and in the presence of Mr.
Boyes made arrangements with me to call at 7.30 or 8 o'clock.

15

在我被拘留期间，我的妻子几乎每天都被叫到德国领事馆，接受各种询问，她说她不知道我做了什么，因为我从未向她透露过我的任何事务。她多次提到，艾廷格（Ettinger）在奥地利领事馆忙于制造针对我的证人证言，但这些证人并不适格。三周后，大约在 9 月 7 日，奥地利当局释放了我，条件是我未经他们许可不得离开上海，并且不得对两国政府发表言论或进行任何形式的报复。在宣誓遵守这些条件后，我被释放。我要求他们在报纸上刊登我无辜被捕的事实，以便恢复我的名誉。他们拒绝这样做，并表示如果德国和奥地利侨民看到我获得自由，他们就会明白我没有犯下任何罪行。为了与西格涅上尉联系，我找到博伊斯和马塞特公司（Boyes & Masset）的博伊斯（Boyes）先生，请他打电话给西格涅上尉，说我想见他。他照办了，西格涅上尉来到博伊斯和马塞特公司的办公地点见我。西格涅上尉表示很高兴看到我摆脱麻烦，我向他大致解释了被捕的原因。西格涅上尉询问了我的财务状况，并承诺寄给我 200 两银子，他也确实这样做了。由于我一直与日本军火经纪人保持联系，在我获释两三天后，一名日本经纪人来找我，问我是否认识任何想买弹药的人。我说“认识”，并与他约定在晚上 7:30 或 8:00 见面。与此同时，我通过博伊斯先生将此事告知了西格涅上尉，据我所知，西格涅上尉与希尔顿·约翰逊（Hilton Johnson）上尉进行了联系，事实上，当天下午，一名公共租界侦探来找我，在博伊斯先生的见证下，与我安排好在 7:30 或 8:00

in the evening at my house No.39 North Soochow Road where
I was expecting a Japanese broker. The Japanese Broker
came and I went with him and a Detective followed us to
Helen Terrace North Szechun Road Extension where I was intro-
duced to the supposed Japanese owner. It took over half an
hour to make arrangements with them. They told me the
ammunition was not there but in Nanzing Road. When I came
out I did not see the Detective. I went with the Japanese
where I convinced myself of the existence of the ammunition.
I then went back to Helen Terrace to find the detective but
could not see him anywhere. I had promised to bring the buyer
at 10 p.m. I went to the North Szechun Road Police Station
where I enquired about the Detective. The Sergeant on
duty a thin person with a lame leg pretended to know all about
it and I told him I wished to see the detective. I do not
remember his name. He rang him up on the phone and I gave
him all necessary instructions. The Police made a raid
on the house about 10.30 the same evening in Nanzing Road
just behind Ettinger's house. The raid was carried out
so badly that the Japanese had time to remove most of the
ammunition and the Police only found a few Brownings and
some ammunition, this I heard the next day. One or two
Japanese were charged for being unlawfully in possession
of arms, one I believe got two months. The next day a
Japanese woman went to my Consul and reported to him that
I was working for the British Authorities, and told him
what had happened the previous evening. As a matter of
fact the public were warned in the Japanese papers that a
man of the name of Max Kindler was a British Government
spy. My Consul called me and asked me about it and told me
that a woman had come to him complaining about me and gave me
to understand that he knew everything about my doings and there
was not a single thing which I had done or will do that was
not known to him. I denied everything and asked him.

16
晚上到我位于苏州河北路 39 号的家中，我预计一名日本经纪人会去那里。日本经纪人来了，我随他而去，一名侦探跟随我们到了北四川路延伸段的海伦台（Helen Terrace），在那里我被介绍给所谓的日本业主。与他们达成协议花了一个多小时。他们告诉我弹药不在那里，而在南京路。当我出来时，我没看到那名侦探。我随日本人去了那里，确认了弹药的存在。然后我回到海伦台寻找那名侦探，但到处都找不到他。我曾答应在晚上 10 点带买家来。我去了北四川路警察局，询问那名侦探的情况。值班警长是个瘦子，腿有点瘸，假装对一切都很了解，我告诉他我想见那名侦探。我不记得他的名字了。他用电话联系了那名侦探，我给出了所有必要的指示。警察大约在当晚 10:30 突袭了南京路的一所房子，就在艾廷格房子的后面。这次突袭执行得非常糟糕，日本人有时间转移大部分弹药，警察只发现了几支勃朗宁手枪和一些弹药，这是我第二天听到的。一两名日本人因非法持有武器被起诉，我相信其中一人被判两个月监禁。第二天，一名日本妇女去找我的领事，向他报告我为英国当局工作，并告诉他前一天晚上发生的事情。事实上，日本报纸警告公众，一个叫马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）的人是英国政府间谍。我的领事叫我过去，询问此事，并告诉我有一名妇女来向他投诉我，还让我明白他知道我的一切行为，我所做或将做的每一件事他都了如指掌。我否认了一切，并问他。

17
for proof and he said that the day would come when he would
have proof in his hands. I replied that when he got that
he could punish me. I then left. I found out later that
the Japanese woman was one kept by a man named Kornilin a
German subject. I believe he is no longer protected by
the German Consulate. I informed Captain Selgme about every-
thing that had happened and I continued my best to obtain
information for Captain Selgme. As the Austrian and German
Community were suspicious of me it was very difficult for me to
find out anything. One day when I came into the Club,
the Secretary of the Austrian Consulate informed me that
several members objected to me and that I had better stay
away. As Rottman saw that I could not give any more
information to Captain Selgme he approached me about January
of this year and asked me to confirm everything he said.
In fact he asked me to put a story together as follows:-
"That there exists a system of basis for submarines and
other hostile bases in Batavia." He asked me to say that
I had heard this. He told me a great deal more but
I cannot remember all he said. I said I would not do so.
He told me he was my superior and if I did not do so he would
try and get me out of Captain Selgme's good graces. He
said if I listened to him and did as he told me he could
obtain more money and I could still remain on the same
good terms with Captain Selgme. I repeated that I could
not do it. I then informed Captain Selgme about it.
I also told Mrs Boyes that Rottman wanted me to repeat
stories which I did not and could not repeat. After that
Rottman got angry with me and tried to do me every possible
harm. As a matter of fact in the Savoy Hotel (about
February) I went into one room where I thought I could get
information for Captain Selgme, and as I came into the
room I found Rottman. When I went in he went out. After
about 5 minutes he came back and in the presence of 4 or 5
gentlemen he made statements showing me to be one of the

作为证据，他说总有一天他会把证据掌握在手中。我回答说，等他拿到证据后，他可以惩罚我。随后我便离开了。后来我得知，那名日本女子是由一名名为 Kornilin 的德国籍男子包养的。我相信他已不再受德国领事馆的保护。我将发生的一切告知了塞尔格姆（Selgme）上尉，并继续尽力为塞尔格姆上尉获取情报。由于奥地利和德国侨民社群对我心存疑忌，我很难打听到任何消息。有一天，当我进入俱乐部时，奥地利领事馆秘书通知我，有几名成员对我表示反对，我最好回避。由于罗特曼（Rottman）看出我无法再向塞尔格姆上尉提供情报，他在今年一月左右接近我，要求我证实他所说的一切。实际上，他要求我编造如下故事：“在巴达维亚存在一个潜艇基地及其他敌对基地的基础体系。”他要求我声称我曾听说过此事。他还告诉了我许多其他内容，但我无法记起他所说的全部内容。我说我不会这样做。他说他是我的上级，如果我不照办，他会设法让我失去塞尔格姆上尉的信任。他说，如果我听他的话并按他的吩咐去做，他能弄到更多的钱，而我仍可与塞尔格姆上尉保持良好的关系。我重申我不能这样做。随后我将此事告知了塞尔格姆上尉。我还告诉博伊斯（Boyes）夫人，罗特曼想让我复述那些我并未听说且无法复述的故事。此后，罗特曼对我勃然大怒，并试图尽一切可能伤害我。事实上，在萨伏伊酒店（Savoy Hotel）（大约在二月），我走进一个房间，以为可以从那里为塞尔格姆上尉获取情报，当我进入房间时，发现了罗特曼。我进去时，他便出去了。大约5分钟后，他回来了，并在四五位绅士面前发表言论，将我描绘成

pages.en:
18
worst characters in the world. He said I took money from
Captain Seigne, that I was a British Spy, he could prove
it by the cheques he cashed for me and other matters of a
similar nature. The people I was with were Russian and Turks
known to Ettinger. I did not reply, I waited for a while
and Rottman went out. The persons there told him,
that as he had spoken to let me say something, then Rottman
went out. I went to Captain Seigne and told him about
this. The same evening two Austrians came to me at
my office and told me to be careful as I was playing with
fire and if the Austrian Authorities listened to what
Rottman had told them I would get into a Hell of a fix.
I begged them not to say anything more and I denied
everything. One day after this I found out that there
was a wireless on the Austrian steamers. I told this
to Captain Seigne and as I was coming out of Captain
Seigne's office I saw Rottman speaking to a man with a
beard, he (Rottman) was very angry with me and called me
names. I reported the incident to Captain Seigne later
and he told me it was alright. I have not spoken to
Rottman for about 5 months. I heard about Ettinger's
arrest about the first or second of June. I happened to
be walking in Yangtsepoo about 6.30 on 6 p.m. and was
stopped by a lady who asked me if I was Mr. Kindler.
She told me to be careful as Rottman had told her that he
would injure me in any way he could.

世界上最恶劣的人物之一。他说我从塞涅（Seigne）上尉那里拿钱，说我是英国间谍，他可以通过为我兑现的支票以及其他类似事项来证明这一点。当时与我在一起的是埃廷格（Ettinger）认识的俄罗斯人和土耳其人。我没有回应，等待了一会儿，罗特曼便出去了。在场的人告诉他，既然他已经说了话，就让我说点什么，随后罗特曼走了出去。我去找塞涅上尉，将此事告诉了他。当晚，两名奥地利人来到我的办公室，告诫我要小心，因为我这是在玩火，如果奥地利当局听信罗特曼对他们说的话，我会陷入极大的困境。我恳求他们不要再说什么，并否认了一切。在此之后的一天，我发现奥地利轮船上装有无线电设备。我将此事告诉了塞涅上尉，当我从塞涅上尉的办公室出来时，看见罗特曼正在与一名留胡子的男子交谈，他（罗特曼）对我非常愤怒，并对我恶语相向。后来我向塞涅上尉报告了这一事件，他说没关系。我已经大约有5个月没有和罗特曼说过话了。我是在6月1日或2日左右听说埃廷格被捕的消息的。当时我碰巧在下午6点30分左右走在杨树浦（Yangtsepoo），被一位女士拦住，她问我是否是金德勒（Kindler）先生。她告诫我要小心，因为罗特曼曾告诉她，他会尽其所能伤害我。

C. I. D.
I. O. REG.
No. 1265
28/9/17

Statement of Max Kindler, 8th June 1917.

I am a Dentist residing lately at 34 Nanking Road,
(above Boyes Basset & Co). I sold my office two months
ago to Dr.Cameron, since when I have been residing at 63
Broadway Terrace, but for the last two days at the French
Hotel.

I was born in Braela in Roumania in 1886, my father being
Austrian and my mother Dutch. I was educated in Vienna and
Berlin. I took my Dental Degrees in Berlin. After I got
my degrees I practiced in Vienna as an Assistant in 1906
for 8 months. From Vienna I went to Bucharest. I remained
in Bucharest for 13 or 14 months during the Exposition. In
Bucharest I was a Dental Surgeon assisting Dr.Lempard (Dentist
de la Court Royal). From Bucharest I travelled for about 5
months through the Holy Land, Turkey, Greece and Egypt. I
settled in Egypt (1908) where I was first an assistant to Dr.
Baoor in Alexandria. After some time I became acquainted
with Lt.Col. Maxwell, R.A.M.C. and through his influence I
became a Dental Surgeon in the Mustapha Pasha Barracks Ramle
Alexandria. I was there for over a year. After that I went
to Madras, India. This was in November 1911. In Madras I
became Dental Surgeon to General Hospital in Madras, my
superior being Major Badcock R.A.M.C. I remained in this
employ for about 4 or 5 months and then I established myself
at Montrode, Madras. Major Badcock was displeased at my
leaving; and only gave me a certificate "for a few weeks". I
remained in Madras until 1913 when I sold my goodwill to a
Dr.Halar for R.2000. From there I returned to Egypt, in
February 1913 where I was seeking employment but could not
get a suitable position. In the beginning of 1914 I bought
a whole Dental outfit at Alexandria(receipts produced).
I remained the whole time in either Alexandria or Cairo.
In the beginning of 1914 I went to Singapore and established
myself in Battery Road, Macalisters Building. I had spent

第1265号
1917年9月28日

马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）陈述，1917年6月8日。

我是一名牙医，最近居住在南京路34号（博伊斯·巴塞特公司 Boyes Basset & Co 楼上）。两个月前我将诊所卖给了卡梅伦（Cameron）医生，此后我一直居住在百老汇大厦63号，但最近两天住在法兰西酒店。

我于1886年出生在罗马尼亚的布拉伊拉（Braela），父亲是奥地利人，母亲是荷兰人。我在维也纳和柏林接受教育。我在柏林获得了牙科学位。获得学位后，我于1906年在维也纳作为一名助手执业8个月。从维也纳我去了布加勒斯特。在博览会期间，我在布加勒斯特停留了13或14个月。在布加勒斯特，我担任牙科外科医生，协助兰帕德（Lempard）医生（皇家宫廷牙医）。离开布加勒斯特后，我花了大约5个月时间游历圣地、土耳其、希腊和埃及。我定居在埃及（1908年），起初在亚历山大港担任鲍尔（Baoor）医生的助手。过了一段时间，我结识了皇家陆军医疗 Corps（R.A.M.C.）的麦克斯韦（Maxwell）中校，通过他的影响，我成为亚历山大港拉姆莱（Ramle）穆斯塔法帕夏兵营的牙科外科医生。我在那里待了一年多。之后我去了印度马德拉斯。那是1911年11月。在马德拉斯，我成为马德拉斯总医院的牙科外科医生，我的上级是皇家陆军医疗 Corps 的巴德科克（Badcock）少校。我受雇于此大约4或5个月，然后在马德拉斯的蒙特罗德（Montrode）自立门户。巴德科克少校对我的离职感到不满；只给我开具了一份“为期几周”的证明。我留在马德拉斯直到1913年，当时我将商誉以2000卢比的价格卖给了一位哈拉尔（Halar）医生。从那里我于1913年2月返回埃及，在那里寻找工作，但未能找到合适的职位。1914年初，我在亚历山大港购买了一整套牙科设备（已出示收据）。在此期间，我一直待在亚历山大港或开罗。1914年初，我前往新加坡，在麦克阿里斯特大楼（Macalisters Building）的电池路（Battery Road）自立门户。我已花费
